t: You're looking at Crocker's Folly, a Grade II* listed former pub on Aberdeen Place in St John's Wood. It was built in 1898 as The Crown, to designs by the architect Charles Worley, in a Northern Renaissance style. It is best known for its elaborate interior, with a great deal of decorative marble. It took the name Crocker's Folly in 1987, after a long-standing nickname. The pub closed in 2004, and since 2014 the building has reopened as a Lebanese restaurant and bar. Worley lived from 1853 to 1906.
